text:
B: Hello, there we go. Can you hear me alright?
A: Yeah, I can hear you. Hiya, I'm Megan.
B: Darren. Nice to meet you, Megan. Where are you, then?
A: Stockton-on-Tees, in the North East. Well, Norton, which is just next to it. What about you?
B: Kesgrave, just outside Ipswich. Suffolk. Bit of a trek from you.
A: Yeah, I've never been that far down that side, I don't think. Erm, so what do you do?
B: Gas engineer. Boilers, mostly. Run me own business, one van, been doing it about fourteen years now.
A: Oh, that's funny, I thought you'd be something like that. You reminded me of my stepdad in your photo. He's an electrician at one of the chemical plants on Teesport.
B: Ha, I'll take that. Proper job, that. Is he alright to live with?
A: He's lovely, yeah. Very calm. Him and my mam have been married eleven years.
B: Good for them. What about you, are you working?
A: I'm a student, second year of diagnostic radiography at Teesside. So I do X-rays, basically, and placements at the hospitals, James Cook and North Tees. It's kind of half lectures and half being on the wards, if that makes sense. I start at half seven on placement, so I'm up at six, and the A19 is a nightmare in the mornings. I was sat in traffic for ages yesterday.
B: Half seven's not too bad, to be fair. I'm usually out the door about then. You drive in, do you?
A: Yeah, I've got a little Corsa. Second-hand, but it does the job.
B: That's all you need. My lad Callum's learning to drive at the minute, seventeen. Lessons are costing a fortune, and the insurance quotes, don't get me started.
A: Oh, my brother's called Callum! He's sixteen though, so not driving yet, thank God. He just eats everything in the fridge.
B: Ha, sounds about right. Mine's the same. You go to the fridge for a bit of ham and it's gone.
A: Exactly that. Is it busy, your job? Like, all the time?
B: Winter's mad. First cold week, everyone's boiler packs up at once. I was doing twelve-hour days in January. Summer's quieter, that's when you do your installs. I did my heat pump ticket a couple of years back as well, 'cause that's where it's all heading, you know.
A: Oh right. Are heat pumps better, then? Sorry, I don't really know anything about them.
B: Erm, they can be. Depends on the house, really. Good insulation, they're great. Old draughty place, you're better off with a decent boiler. I tell people straight what'll work for them.
A: That's good. My stepdad says the same about his job, that people just want someone to tell them what to do.
B: That's half of it, yeah. Keep 'em happy. Do you like the hospital side?
A: I do. I get a bit nervous before placements, but I'm good with the older patients. They're usually more nervous than me, so I just talk them through it. I keep a little notebook in my tunic pocket for all the settings, 'cause I'm worried I'll forget something.
B: Sounds like you're doing it right to me. Better nervous than cocky.
A: Yeah, that's what my supervisor sort of said. Do you watch football? My stepdad has Boro on all the time.
B: Ipswich, yeah. They've done alright lately, been to Portman Road a few times. Good atmosphere.
A: I couldn't name more than about three Boro players, honestly. I just sit there with him.
B: Ha, that's my missus with Ipswich. Right, I think that's us about done.
A: Oh, is it? That went fast. It was nice talking to you, Darren.
B: You too, Megan. Good luck with the placements, yeah.
